added: Más Bandwidth LLC (netcode and reliable, the C beneath dream-net (BSD-3-Clause; a binary that ships it reproduces dream-net's NOTICE.md))
removed: Más Bandwidth LLC (netcode, reliable and serialize, beneath dream-net)

notes.summary: Luau 0.747, which removed the integer type: packed scalars ride in tagged light userdata on x86-64 and AArch64 and in interned userdata elsewhere, each kind is its own nominal type, and every other 64-bit value is an exact number or a Bits64. The transport moves to dream-net 2.1, on Más Bandwidth's C netcode with its handshake nonce fix, and a started child's stdin is fed about ten times faster.
added: `@dream/bits64` in every plan: `fromNumber`, `toNumber` (exact, an error past 2^53), `fromParts`, `parts`, `hex`, `fromHex`, and `read` and `write` on a buffer in little or big byte order. A `Bits64` has no arithmetic.

`l3i::packed::carrier`: one seam for how a packed scalar is stored, checked by a self-test at every runtime creation (every single bit, all ones and the non-canonical patterns through a push, a read, equality, inequality under another tag and a table key). `L3I_CARRIER=boxed` at build time forces the interned carrier on a desktop for testing, without `jit`.
`ffi::luau_loadlazy`, Luau 0.747's loader that builds each function on first call. l3i does not use it.

`Runtime::lint_native_annotations` and `source::lint_native_annotations`: the parameters of native functions whose annotation still compiles to a userdata guard after the packed-kind erasure (a kind missing from `packed_types`, a misspelt type), each with its position. Such a guard refuses a packed scalar on every call and leaves the function at interpreter speed.

Luau 0.747's compiler and code generator fixes are on: `LuauCompileLoopUnrollNegativeZero`, `LuauCodegenExitSyncExpectedTag` and `LuauCodegenFastcallAnalysisLimit`, with 0.746's `LuauCompileRequireNoInline`, `LuauLoadExplicitGcDisable`, `LuauSaltedInterningTable` and `LuauCodegenX64ConflictCheck`.
changed: dream-net runs on Más Bandwidth's C netcode 1.5.0 and reliable, vendored in dream-net and compiled with clang (18 or newer; l3i already builds only with clang), in place of the netcode-official, reliable and serialize-official crates. Those crates leave l3i's dependency graph, and with them netcode-official 1.0.0, which is yanked: a fresh resolution of l3i 2.11.0 or older no longer builds. The wire format above netcode is unchanged.

Every build now links C under BSD-3-Clause (netcode and reliable, Más Bandwidth LLC) and ISC (netcode's libsodium subset), dream-net's license being `(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND BSD-3-Clause AND ISC`. A product that ships l3i reproduces dream-net's `NOTICE.md`.

A started child's stdin (`process.start`, `child:write`) is written in pieces of up to 256 KiB copied out of the queue as slices, where it went 8 KiB at a time, a byte at a time, under the lock `write` needs. Feeding 8 MB frames to a child went from 18.09 ms to 1.83 ms a frame in one build without LTO, so read it as relative: about ten times faster, enough to stream raw 1080p60 video to an encoder. The 1 MiB queue bound, `wouldBlock`, close and cancel behave as before.
Every dependency is at its latest compatible release (cc 1.11, ICU4X 2.4, rustls-webpki 0.103.17, webpki-root-certs 1.0.12, among others). No requirement in the manifest moved but dream-net's.

Luau 0.747 adds about 9 instructions to every C function call on AArch64 (a raw `lua_CFunction` counts 243 against 234 on 0.746 under Cachegrind) and none on x86-64; l3i's own share of a bound call is unchanged. The measurements and how to repeat them are in `CARRIER_BUDGETS.md`.

Native lowering of `@dream/quat`, `@dream/raster` and `@dream/bytes` reads and writes the light carrier directly and checks the kind nibble, so a lowered call stays native. A lowered call that produces a packed value writes three stores where the integer took one (Luau does not track a light userdata's `extra` word), so the smallest such operations cost more than they did: `C:rgba8` 2 to 3 instructions (+10 to 15 percent) and about 65 percent more cycles, `Q:fromXYZW` +2 to +3 percent, a reassigned `acc = Q:mul(acc, r)` about 18 cycles, reassigned raster operations 3 to 5 ns. `C:rgba8` exceeds the 3 percent native budget the migration set and is accepted as an exception until Luau tracks `extra` (#34). Binder instruction counts are unchanged.

On targets other than x86-64 and AArch64 (wasm32 first) a packed scalar is an interned userdata: the same semantics, at the cost of a lookup and, for a new value, an allocation. `jit` is refused there. CI builds `wasm32-unknown-emscripten` and runs the integration suite there under Node with every feature emscripten can back (all but `jit`, `process`, `tcp`, `dns`, `tls`, `bytes-crypto`), but for UDP sockets, child processes, threads and filesystem semantics its Node filesystem lacks; the boxed carrier reproduces the integer carrier's corpus and BufferPack goldens byte for byte. A wasm32 host links with a `-sSTACK_SIZE` well above emscripten's 64 KiB default and with `ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH`.
Packed type names are erased to `any` before bytecode, so native type guards never reject a packed value; analysis still sees the names.
fixed: A lowered colour operation accepted a `Color` whose payload exceeded 32 bits, which the bound call refuses; it now exits to the bound call.
`quat.key`, `keyRotation` and `keyFlags` canonicalized a non-canonical payload where their lowering did not; both now compute on the bits.

`data.selection` with a length the host cannot allocate aborted the process (Rust's infallible allocation); it raises. On 32-bit targets a span's count, offset or stride past the address space was reported as negative or as a short stride; it is refused as a 64-bit target refuses it.

l3i did not build for wasm32: the value mirror pinned a 64-bit `TString` layout (its asserts refused the build rather than misread), the toolchain config handed emscripten's target to plain clang, and the value mirror's self-test compared a light userdata's whole value word where a 32-bit pointer fills half of it, and `data` pinned a 64-bit offset for its selections' word pointer.

`quat.mul`, `slerp` and `rotate` (module and `quat.math()`) agreed with their native lowering only to the angle: the bound path decoded, renormalised and branched differently. They now run the lowering's operations in its order and return the same bits; results from well-formed rotations are unchanged.

`process.run` could answer `held = true` with whole captures: a process holding a capture that wrote and exited just as the run gave up on it after 250 ms quiet had its output read, but the run still said held. `held` now says a reader was stopped before its stream's end (#37).
breaking: dream-net 2.1.0 (from 1.1.1). `@dream/udp` speaks NETCODE 1.03, which fixes AEAD nonce reuse in the netcode handshake (GHSA-8mrq-q9c6-h23v): a peer on l3i 3.0 never connects to one on l3i 2.x, whose dream-net speaks NETCODE 1.02, and the attempt ends in `connectFailed` with `"timeout"`. Upgrade servers and clients together.

Connect tokens admit one session: once a session is established with a token, the server refuses it again, from any address, even after the session ends. A client that reconnects needs a fresh token from `server:connectToken`. A server created from Luau still accepts a token minted in the second it started; a host-created `dream_net::Server` keeps the restart floor dream-net 2.0 added (a token expiring within the server's maximum token lifetime of its start is refused, 30 seconds with `Server::new`).

A Rust host that depends on dream-net itself, to build the `dream_net::Server` it hands `udp::Server::new`, moves to dream-net 2.1.0 too, since that is the `Server` the bridge takes, and gets dream-net 2's types: `Error::Netcode` and `generate_connect_token` carry `dream_net::NetcodeError`, and `TransportConfig::reliable_config` and `Connection::reliable_counters` return `ReliableConfig` and `ReliableCounters`. Reliable's packet buffers are capped at 16384.

Luau 0.747 (from 0.745). The `integer` type, `42i` literals, the `integer` library and `buffer.readinteger`/`writeinteger` are gone from the language: `42i` is a syntax error (`Malformed number`) and `integer` an unknown type to the checker.

Fast flags: the integer flags left with the type, and `LuauCompileNoFoldVectorEqW`, `LuauCompileMoveElision`, `LuauCompileFastpcall`, `LuauFastpcall`, `LuauTableRobustOom` and `LuauCodegenPropagateFallbackTags` graduated and left the list, so `memory::fast_flag` answers `None` for them. The while-local flags lost their `Debug` prefix (`LuauExperimentalWhileLocalSyntax`, `LuauExperimentalWhileLocalAnalysis`).

A packed scalar is no longer a Luau integer. `typeof` answers its kind's name (`Quaternion`, `AnimationKey`, `Color`, `ClipRect`, `Color16`, `Bits64`, a host kind's `NAME`); it compares and keys tables by its 64 bits and kind, and arithmetic or ordering on one raises. Its bits are unchanged, so `BufferPack` bytes, saved files and wire formats read the same.

Signatures and definitions name each packed kind as a nominal type instead of `integer`, so a strict script that passes a `Color` where a `Quaternion` is expected no longer type checks. A plan whose userdata class or type alias takes a kind's name does not finalize.
The packed constants (`quat.IDENTITY`, raster's `TRANSPARENT`, `BLACK`, `WHITE`, `CLIP_ALL` and the three 16-bit colours) are module values, no longer folded by the compiler.

`@dream/udp`: peer, event and channel ids are numbers, exact or an error, never rounded; the protocol id, client ids and connect-token fingerprint halves are `Bits64`. `udp.server{ protocolId = ... }` takes a `Bits64` (`bits64.fromNumber(n)` or `bits64.fromHex(s)`).

`@dream/bytes`: `readVarint` and `readSignedVarint` answer an exact number or raise above 2^53, and `readVarint64`/`writeVarint64` carry all 64 bits as a `Bits64`; `readi64be`/`writei64be`, `fnv1a64`, `xxh64`, `xxh3` and a 64-bit hasher's `value()` are `Bits64`. 32-bit checksums stay numbers.

Rust: `convert::Integer`, `FieldValue::Integer`, `CompileConstant::Integer`, `stack::Type::Integer`, `ValueView::is_integer`, `Library::Integer` and the integer arms of the number readers are gone; `Library::STANDARD` has 11 entries. `Bits64` is a wide packed scalar. `FieldValue::Bits64` replaces `FieldValue::Integer` where the light carrier is in use.

Rust FFI: Luau 0.747 renumbers the type tags after `LUA_TNUMBER` (`LUA_TVECTOR` is 4 through `LUA_TOBJECT` 12), and the integer entry points (`lua_pushinteger64`, `lua_tointeger64`, `lua_isinteger64`, `luaL_checkinteger64`, `luaL_optinteger64`, `luaopen_integer`, `luau_set_compile_constant_integer64`, `lua_userdatadirectfield_setinteger64`) are gone.
Host light userdata: `LightUserdata` pushes and `set_light_userdata_name` refuse tags at or above 128, which packed kinds own, and a pointer with a non-zero top nibble.
`@dream/luau` trees: `ExprConstantInteger` is gone, a `StatClass` name is a `Local` or an `Expr` (Luau 0.747's `class a.b`), and `TypeTable` lost `isExact` with Luau's exact table types.

Bytecode with a 64-bit integer constant, which an l3i built on Luau 0.746 or older could write, is refused by `load_bytecode` with an error naming the chunk. Luau 0.747 keeps bytecode version 14, so its own version check would not catch it.
notes.migration:
Rebuild every bytecode cache: a chunk with an integer constant is refused, and chunks without one load but were compiled with the old flags.

Scripts that wrote integer literals write numbers (`7` for `7i`) where the value is a count or a size, and `bits64.fromNumber(n)` or `bits64.fromHex(s)` where it is an id or a hash. `typeof(x) == "integer"` checks become `typeof(x) == "Quaternion"` (or the kind expected). Comparing a udp client id or a digest with a number never succeeds; compare it with another `Bits64`.

Hosts that pushed light userdata with tags at or above 128, or with high pointer bits set, move those tags below 128. A host that matched on `stack::Type::Integer`, read `convert::Integer` or set `CompileConstant::Integer` uses numbers or `Bits64` instead.

Packed values written to files, buffers or sockets keep their bytes; nothing needs converting.

Ship servers and clients built on 3.0 together: they do not connect to 2.x peers. Mint a new connect token for every connection attempt, and keep none to present again after a reconnect or a restart. A Rust host that matched netcode-official's `Error` matches `dream_net::NetcodeError`, which has the same variants and texts.
